qualification: local A05.3 rejected directional diagnostics experiment; not A05.3 closure, cross-host, G1-G5, or release qualification

candidate.scope: Split the existing compiler-ABI rejection counter into legacy-to-tier-one, tier-one-to-legacy, and other directional counters without changing chain-target admission policy.
candidate.behavioralIntent: Diagnostics-only refinement of the already accepted coarse chain-target rejection histogram.
candidate.productionFinding: Two runs of the identical release binary terminated before emitting terminal output or a diagnostic receipt. Because admission policy was unchanged and the deterministic aggregate passed, this is a reproducible layout-sensitive host-side reliability failure, not evidence that either directional count is safe to retain or infer.

verification.deterministicAggregate: 1,555 tests in 179 suites passed with test parallelism disabled; the environment-driven pinned boot test skipped because its variables were absent, then the frozen fixture was executed explicitly.

retainedBaseline.reason: The coarser instrumentation completed the pinned workload and reconciled all target attempts; it remains the production-safe ranking.

disposition.reason: The directional counters do not survive the production reliability gate and are fully reverted. Directionality must be measured out of process or through an otherwise binary-layout-neutral mechanism before it can guide a bridge implementation.

limitations: No diagnostic receipt or terminal output survived either attempt, so elapsed time, instruction count, and exact termination status are intentionally not fabricated.
The repeated failure establishes candidate unreliability but does not identify its underlying mechanism.
The accepted coarse histogram ranks compiler-ABI mismatch first but does not reveal direction.
